title: Complete and complementary cat food
text: Cats Protection recommends food labelled complete because it supplies the nutrients a cat needs. Complementary products, including treats, do not provide a balanced diet by themselves. Food should suit the cat's life stage. Homemade meals are not recommended unless a veterinarian advises them for a medical reason.
summary_cn: 选标明 complete 的食品；complementary 食品不能单独充当均衡主食。
source_section: What should I feed my cat?

title: Changing a cat's food gradually
text: Cats Protection advises offering a small amount of new food beside the usual food in separate bowls, rather than mixing them. If the cat accepts it, increase the new food and reduce the old food over a week or longer. If the cat refuses it or becomes unwell, retain the old food and seek veterinary advice.
summary_cn: 该指南建议新旧粮分碗提供，并用一周或更久逐步过渡；不接受或不适时咨询兽医。
source_section: Changing your cat's food

title: Water bowls and drinking preferences
text: Cats Protection suggests wide ceramic, metal or glass water bowls so whiskers are not pressed against the sides. Keep water separate from food and litter trays, and offer bowls in several locations. Some cats prefer moving water. A sudden change in drinking should be checked by a veterinarian.
summary_cn: 宽口陶瓷、金属或玻璃碗，多处提供并远离食物和猫砂盆；饮水突然变化需检查。
source_section: How much should my cat be drinking?

title: Water rather than milk
text: Cats need continuous access to clean drinking water. Cats Protection advises against cow's milk and human milk alternatives: many cats cannot digest lactose well, and alternatives may contain unsuitable ingredients. Commercial cat milk is an occasional high-calorie treat, not a replacement for water or a balanced diet.
summary_cn: 水应持续供应；牛奶及人用替代奶不推荐，猫奶也不能代替水或均衡饮食。
source_section: What do cats drink?; Do cats drink milk?

title: Litter tray quantity and placement
text: Cats Protection recommends one litter tray for each cat plus one additional tray. Put trays in separate quiet, accessible locations, away from food, water and sleeping areas. Avoid noisy appliances and busy passageways. A row of neighbouring trays is not equivalent to distributing them. Cats with mobility difficulties benefit from low-sided trays.
summary_cn: 每只猫一个盆，再额外加一个；分散放在安静、易到达的位置，行动困难的猫用低边盆。
source_section: Where to put your cat's litter tray; The best litter tray for your cat

title: Cleaning litter trays
text: Cats Protection advises removing urine and faeces twice daily, or more often if needed. Empty and wash the tray with hot soapy water or a cat-safe cleaner at least weekly. Covered trays may need thorough cleaning more often because they retain smells. Avoid newspaper or plastic liners inside the tray.
summary_cn: 每天至少清理排泄物两次，每周至少彻底清洗一次；封闭盆可能需更频繁清洗。
source_section: How to clean your cat's litter tray

title: Introducing gentle grooming
text: Long-haired cats and cats unable to groom themselves may need brushing assistance. Cats Protection recommends introducing brushes gradually, working a little at a time and using minimal restraint. A sudden increase or decrease in self-grooming warrants a veterinary appointment, rather than assuming it is only a grooming preference.
summary_cn: 梳毛应逐步适应、少量进行，减少强制固定；自我梳理突然增减应预约兽医。
source_section: Do I need to groom my cat?; How to get your cat used to being groomed

title: A quiet room for a newly adopted cat
text: Before releasing a new cat from its carrier, Cats Protection recommends preparing a quiet room. Include separate food and water areas, a private litter tray far from both, a hiding place, a secure elevated resting spot, a bed, a scratching post and toys. This provides space to settle before exploring the whole home.
summary_cn: 先准备安静房间，配齐分开的食水、猫砂盆、躲藏处、高处、床、抓柱和玩具。
source_section: Setting up your cat's new space

title: Allowing a new cat time to settle
text: Cats Protection advises patience when a cat enters a new home; do not pressure it to interact or explore before it is ready. Initial hiding or avoidance can occur during adjustment. Look for gradual improvement rather than expecting every cat to settle at the same speed. Prolonged stress without improvement should prompt veterinary advice.
summary_cn: 不要强迫新猫互动，不同猫适应速度不同；观察逐步改善，持续压力无改善需咨询兽医。
source_section: When your cat first arrives home; Signs your cat is struggling to settle

title: Choosing a scratching surface
text: For claw-maintenance scratching, Cats Protection recommends a stable post tall enough for a full stretch, initially beside the scratched furniture. A horizontal pad can suit cats that scratch carpets. Once accepted, move it gradually. Provide separate posts for different cats; scratching linked to anxiety also requires attention to the source of stress.
summary_cn: 抓柱需稳定且足够高，先放在被抓家具附近；偏好横向抓挠的猫可用抓板。
source_section: Prevent your cat from scratching your furniture

title: Short play sessions and toy safety
text: Cats Protection says games lasting one or two minutes can be useful. Rotate toys to sustain interest and let a cat catch a wand toy occasionally. Inspect toys for damage. Do not leave a cat unsupervised with toys it might shred, swallow or become tangled in.
summary_cn: 一两分钟的短游戏也有价值，轮换玩具并让猫偶尔捕获；有吞咽或缠绕风险的玩具需看护。
source_section: How to play with your cat; How often should I play with my cat?

title: Redirecting rough play away from hands
text: Cats Protection discourages using fingers or toes as play targets. Use toys that keep hunting activity away from the body, such as wand toys or thrown balls. Regular play is particularly important indoors. Newly appearing play aggression in an adult cat should be checked by a veterinarian before seeking behavioural help.
summary_cn: 用逗猫棒或球代替手脚；成年猫突然出现攻击性玩耍时，先排查医疗原因。
source_section: How can I teach my cat to play gently?; Is my cat's play too rough?

title: Introducing cats in stages
text: Cats Protection describes staged introductions: a separate sanctuary room, scent exchange using cloths, visual contact through a glass barrier, then mesh-barrier contact before short face-to-face meetings. Progress only when cats are comfortable with the preceding stage. Do not force approach or meetings, and provide ways to retreat or reach a high place.
summary_cn: 先独立房间，再交换气味、隔玻璃与网栏接触，最后短时见面；不强迫并保留退路。
source_section: Introducing cats or kittens: the basic steps

title: Reducing competition in multi-cat homes
text: Cats Protection recommends separate food and water bowls, beds, litter trays and hiding or sleeping places for each cat, with spare resources. Avoid placing essentials in busy shared areas or too close to another cat. Cats can experience tension without fighting. Sudden aggression in a normally calm cat should be discussed with a veterinarian.
summary_cn: 为各猫分开配置资源并留备用；没有打架也可能有压力，突然攻击应咨询兽医。
source_section: Cats living together; How to help your cats get along

title: Selecting a secure cat carrier
text: Cats Protection recommends a sturdy, secure carrier that is easy to clean and allows comfortable lying and repositioning. Ventilation openings should be present on at least two sides. A removable top can help with handling and training. Transport cats in a carrier rather than loose in a car.
summary_cn: 箱体稳固、可清洁、可舒适调整姿势，至少两侧通风；乘车不能让猫自由散放。
source_title: Choosing and Using a Cat Carrier
source_section: What is the best type of cat carrier to buy?; Why do you need a cat carrier?

title: Removing hazards from a cat's room
text: Cats Protection recommends a private starting space kept away from dogs, children and guests. Remove cleaning products and objects that could be knocked over. Add a hiding place and the cat's essential resources, together with enrichment such as puzzle toys, wand toys or cardboard boxes.
summary_cn: 初始空间保持私密，清走清洁剂及易被打翻的物品，加入躲藏处、必需品与活动用品。
source_title: Preparing Your Home For a Cat
source_section: Here's a step-by-step guide on setting up a space for your new cat

title: Storing dry and opened canned food
text: Cornell recommends storing dry cat food in a cool, dry place, checking its expiry date and using an airtight container to help preserve nutrients and flavour. Prolonged storage can degrade vitamins and allow fats to become rancid. Refrigerate unused portions of opened canned food to preserve quality and reduce spoilage.
summary_cn: 干粮阴凉干燥密封保存并检查到期日；开封罐头的未用部分应冷藏。
publisher: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
source_section: Types of Commercial Cat Food: Dry Food; Canned Food

title: Loss of appetite needs veterinary assessment
text: Cornell explains that appetite loss is a sign with many possible physical or psychological causes, rather than a diagnosis. A cat that is not eating deserves veterinary assessment. Persistent food refusal can cause serious harm, especially in very young kittens. An owner should not assume the cat is merely choosing to be difficult.
summary_cn: 食欲丧失是症状而非诊断；不进食应接受兽医评估，幼猫尤其脆弱。
publisher: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
source_section: Main article: causes and veterinary assessment

title: Breathing difficulty requires immediate help
text: Cornell identifies difficult breathing, unusually rapid breathing and noisy open-mouth breathing as possible signs of respiratory distress. Breathing difficulty is a clinical sign, not a specific diagnosis. If a cat cannot breathe comfortably, seek veterinary help immediately rather than trying to resolve it at home; determining the cause requires professional examination.
summary_cn: 呼吸困难及张口喘气等可提示呼吸窘迫，应立即求助；不能据此自行诊断或在家处理。
publisher: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
source_section: Main article: signs of dyspnea and advice to owners

title: Straining with little or no urine
text: Cornell describes repeated attempts to urinate, straining and little or no urine as signs that can occur with urethral obstruction. Other urinary problems can look similar, so symptoms alone cannot establish a diagnosis. Suspected obstruction requires immediate veterinary attention because it is potentially life-threatening. Male cats have greater obstruction risk.
summary_cn: 反复用力却几乎无尿可能涉及尿道阻塞，疑似阻塞应立即求助；相似症状不能自行确诊。
publisher: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
source_section: Urethral Obstruction
